# The live V2-vs-V3 question bank

**84 questions** across 30 categories, plus **10 controlled behaviour cases**. Generated by `scripts/build_cockpit_question_bank.py`; the machine-readable copy is `tests/evals/cockpit_agentic/question_bank.json`.

## What this is for, and what it is not

Run the same questions against the preserved Cockpit V2 branch and against this one, with a real credential, and have a credit person read the two answers side by side.

It is not a scoring harness and it deliberately carries no expected answers. For most of these there is no single right number, and a bank that shipped one would be grading the model against whatever its author happened to believe.

What each entry carries instead is the BEHAVIOUR that must hold whatever the analysis says: this must be answered from the Cockpit, this must be referred and execute nothing, this must ask before choosing between PIT and TTC. Those are the application's responsibility and they are checkable without a credit judgement.

**Nothing here is graded until a real provider credential is available.** A mock cannot answer any of these.

## Expected behaviours

| Behaviour | Meaning | Count |
|---|---|---:|
| `answer_from_cockpit` | Answered from the twenty-quarter Cockpit domain | 61 |
| `ask_before_choosing` | Ask before choosing between stored fields that answer differently | 6 |
| `refer_and_execute_nothing` | Refer to the owning functionality and execute nothing | 10 |
| `say_the_data_is_not_there` | Say the data is not there; do not interpolate or benchmark | 4 |
| `refuse_the_other_domain` | Refuse the other domain, without revealing its schema | 3 |

## The questions


### PD trend and history

| id | lang | question | expected | what to check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pd-trend-01` | en | How has the PIT 12-month PD moved across the last eight quarters for the construction sector? | `answer_from_cockpit` | Twenty quarters exist; eight were asked for. The answer must not silently widen to all twenty. |
| `pd-trend-02` | en | Which borrowers have seen their through-the-cycle lifetime PD rise in every one of the last four quarters? | `answer_from_cockpit` | Monotonic rise across four consecutive quarters, not a first-to-last comparison. |
| `pd-trend-03` | en | Show the distribution of 12-month PIT PD by IFRS 9 stage in the latest quarter. | `answer_from_cockpit` | Stage is a facility attribute; the grain must not repeat borrowers. |
| `pd-trend-04` | en | What was the largest single-quarter increase in PIT 12-month PD in the whole history, and for which facility? | `answer_from_cockpit` | Across twenty quarters and every facility position. |

### PIT versus TTC

| id | lang | question | expected | what to check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pit-ttc-01` | en | How far apart are the point-in-time and through-the-cycle 12-month PDs in the latest quarter, and where is the gap widest? | `answer_from_cockpit` | Both are stored fields. Neither may be derived from the other. |
| `pit-ttc-02` | en | Has the PIT-to-TTC ratio for the manufacturing sector widened or narrowed over the last two years? | `answer_from_cockpit` | Two years is eight quarters of the twenty. |
| `pit-ttc-03` | en | What is the average PD for my portfolio? | `ask_before_choosing` | PIT or TTC, 12-month or lifetime -- four stored fields answer this and the question chose none. Ask; do not pick. |

### 12-month versus lifetime

| id | lang | question | expected | what to check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `horizon-01` | en | For stage 2 facilities, how much larger is lifetime PD than 12-month PD on a point-in-time basis? | `answer_from_cockpit` | Lifetime is a survival curve here, not twelve-month times the years. |
| `horizon-02` | en | Which facilities have a lifetime PD more than five times their 12-month PD, and what are their remaining maturities? | `answer_from_cockpit` | Requires the stored lifetime horizon, not an assumed one. |
| `horizon-03` | en | Give me the monthly PD term structure for facility F-000123. | `say_the_data_is_not_there` | The domain is quarterly and stores a lifetime horizon in months, not a monthly curve. Say so rather than interpolating one. |

### ECL movement and decomposition

| id | lang | question | expected | what to check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ecl-01` | en | How much did reported ECL move between the two latest quarters, and what drove it? | `answer_from_cockpit` | 'What drove it' is the model's analysis to construct. There is no prescribed decomposition in this architecture. |
| `ecl-02` | en | Split the ECL movement over the last year between stage migration and parameter change. | `answer_from_cockpit` | Stage and parameters are both stored per quarter. Whether the split is clean is the model's to say. |
| `ecl-03` | en | How much of the current ECL is management overlay rather than modelled? | `answer_from_cockpit` | `ecl_overlay` and `ecl_modelled` are separate stored fields. |
| `ecl-04` | en | Does the reported ECL reconcile to PD times LGD times EAD, and where does it not? | `answer_from_cockpit` | It does not, by construction in this release. An answer claiming it does has not looked. |

### Rating migration

| id | lang | question | expected | what to check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rating-01` | en | Which borrowers were downgraded by two notches or more over the last four quarters? | `answer_from_cockpit` | Nineteen ordered grades; a notch is a rank step, not a letter change. |
| `rating-02` | en | Build a rating migration matrix between the first and the latest quarter. | `answer_from_cockpit` | Nineteen by nineteen, borrower grain, no double counting. |
| `rating-03` | en | How many borrowers are rated below BBB- and what share of exposure do they carry? | `answer_from_cockpit` | 'Below' is a rank comparison on the ordered scale, not alphabetical. |

### Covenant deterioration

| id | lang | question | expected | what to check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cov-01` | en | Which covenants are in breach in the latest quarter, and since when? | `answer_from_cockpit` | Breach dates are stored; 'since when' must come from them. |
| `cov-02` | en | Show covenants whose headroom has fallen for three consecutive quarters without yet breaching. | `answer_from_cockpit` | Headroom is stored per test. Obligation grain: a borrower-wide covenant must not be counted once per facility. |
| `cov-03` | en | How many breaches were waived, and how many waivers expire within the next two quarters? | `answer_from_cockpit` | Waiver and cure dates are stored fields. |
| `cov-04` | en | For borrowers with a DSCR covenant, does the tested value agree with the DSCR in their financials? | `answer_from_cockpit` | It should, in this release, and a mismatch is a finding worth reporting rather than smoothing. |

### Collateral coverage and haircuts

| id | lang | question | expected | what to check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `coll-01` | en | What is the net realizable collateral coverage of drawn exposure by sector in the latest quarter? | `answer_from_cockpit` | Post-haircut values, allocated. Summing gross value across the allocation relation double counts a shared asset. |
| `coll-02` | en | Which collateral types carry the largest total haircut, and how is the haircut built up? | `answer_from_cockpit` | Market, liquidity, FX and legal haircuts are stored separately. |
| `coll-03` | en | How much collateral has a valuation older than four quarters or an expired valuation? | `answer_from_cockpit` | Valuation date and expiry date are both stored. |
| `coll-04` | en | Which facilities are secured by assets shared with other facilities, and what is their allocated share? | `answer_from_cockpit` | The allocation relation is the only correct route; the asset relation holds a shared asset once. |

| id | lang | question | expected | what to check |

## Controlled behaviour cases

These do not need a credit judgement. They are the application's guarantees, run against the live models rather than against a mock, and each has a mock-based counterpart in `tests/cockpit_agentic/` that proves the same property structurally.

| id | case | setup | what must hold |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ctrl-01` | First query succeeds | A clean Cockpit question with an unambiguous measure and window. | One submission, one analysis round, an answer. No repair. |
| `ctrl-02` | One failure, then a successful repair | A question whose natural first query names a plausible field that does not exist -- `pd_12_month` rather than `pd_pit_12m`. | One failure, the sixteen context items verified on the outbound request, and a second submission that succeeds. CreditProbe must not have supplied the column. |
| `ctrl-03` | Repeated invalid query, five-submission stop | Force five distinct failing submissions. | The sixth is refused. The stop says five were used and why. The identical-candidate block must fire if the same query is resubmitted, which is a different stop. |
| `ctrl-04` | Three-round sufficiency stop | A question the model keeps revising the plan for. | Three analysis rounds, then a stop that reports what was established and what was not. Not a fourth round under another name. |
| `ctrl-05` | Time-budget stop | Standard mode, a question whose execution runs past 60 seconds. | A stop naming the deadline. Partial work is not presented as an answer. |
| `ctrl-06` | Token-budget stop | A thread long enough to reach the cumulative ceiling. | A stop naming the token budget. The earliest binding limit wins, so check which one actually bound -- at these volumes the spend ceiling reaches first. |
| `ctrl-07` | User cancellation | Cancel mid-execution from the browser. | Execution stops, the sandbox process is killed, the workspace is removed, and the envelope says it was cancelled. |
| `ctrl-08` | Thread summary continuity | Three exchanges, then a follow-up that depends on the first. | The rolling summary carries it. The answer must not silently re-ask. |
| `ctrl-09` | No unnecessary chart | A single-number question. | No chart. A chart on a scalar is decoration. |
| `ctrl-10` | A chart when it is analytically useful | A twenty-quarter trend question. | A chart bound to the actual result rows, not a redrawn approximation. |

## Running it

```
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...  COCKPIT_AGENTIC_V3=true \
    python scripts/cockpit_v3_live_validation.py
```

That script runs the twelve live steps end to end. This bank is the material for the side-by-side review that follows it, and the review is a person's, not a script's.
